Seadown School
Message from the Head
Welcome to Seadown School. It is a privilege to be Headteacher at our small, caring, independent special school for pupils aged 6 to 16 who have a range of needs including SEMH (social, emotional and mental health), autism, ADHD and dyslexia.
We recognise that education has been a challenge for many of our pupils. We pride ourselves on forming positive, trusting and respectful relationships where everyone is valued, and much emphasis is placed on getting to know each pupil as an individual.
We continue to be an OFSTED Good-rated school as of July 2024.
Read the most recent OFSTED report by clicking the logo below.

Seadown School
Our Governors
School governors make a valuable contribution to children’s education, opportunities and futures.
Being a school governor is a challenging but hugely rewarding role. It will give you the chance to make a real difference to young people, give something back to your local community and use and develop your skills in a board-level environment.
Responsibilities of the Governing Body
Our governing body has a strategic role in the development of the school but does not become involved in day-to-day management issues – that is the role of the headteacher. Key responsibilities of the governing body can be summarised as:
Setting and monitoring the school's strategic vision, aims and policies
Reviewing, adopting and monitoring the School Development Plan
Determining how the school's budget is spent (with a focus on Pupil Premium and the impact of its spend)
Setting standards for pupils' behaviour and discipline in consultation with the Headteacher
Working in partnership with the senior leadership team making sure school buildings are welcoming and safe
Review and monitor examination/national test results
Monitor attendance of pupils/staff/governors
Reviewing, adopting and monitoring the SEF
Hearing escalated appeals and grievances
At Seadown School, we are fortunate that we have an extremely dedicated and committed board of governors. All governors can be contacted via the Clerk, Nikki Orchard at nikki.orchard@seadownschool.co.uk
Mr Steve Alexander: Safeguarding /Premises, Health & Safety Governor (Co-opted Governor & Chair)
My name is Steve Alexander I have three children, all grown up now and two grandchildren. I have lived in West Sussex for the best part of 30 years and enjoy the countryside and making good use of the beach in the summer.
I have been involved to some degree in the school from the beginning. I have been fortunate in seeing the school grow from strength to strength. I am proud for the positive impact the school has on the children and their development into young adults. I enjoy being the chair of governors as it allows me to make positive contributions to the school and other people that are also involved in its development.
Dr Michael Rutherford: Teaching & Learning Governor (Parent Governor)
I am a doctor in the local mental health trust working in perinatal psychiatry and have been in the area for the last 7 years. I also work in medical education so have some understanding of teaching which I hope will be helpful in my new role as parent governor.
I am keen to give back and help the school continue in its development, especially with all the recent changes, as I’ve been so impressed with the dedication of the staff and how the children seem to thrive in the environment.
I enjoy running, weightlifting and cooking. I also get my two girls involved in making elderflower champagne and cordial at the right time of the year!
Mrs Tracey Light: Finance Governor (Community Governor)
I am married with 3 grown-up children 3 grandchildren and a Labrador! I enjoy the outdoor life, especially walking and riding my horse on the Knepp Estate in Shipley.
I am really approachable and always happy for a chat.
I have worked in the NHS and now for Local Government starting in Adult Social Care and then in Finance as Senior Finance Officer for several years.
Currently, I am the Locality Lead for Adur & Worthing promoting partnership working with a wide range of stakeholders to support communities to build capacity increase their wellbeing and reach their potential.
One of my key priorities in my working life is to give our children and young people the best start in life, this promoted my decision to become a Governor.
I believe that my background will support and add to the development of the school as it looks towards its future.
I hope to make a positive contribution to the school and every child’s education and play an active role in helping the school to go from strength to strength. I think it is important to create an environment where each child is valued and develops their own self-esteem and confidence, so they can excel both academically and socially.
Mr Hugh MacGregor: (Staff Governor)
I work as the SENCo at Seadown. I have worked in education since I was 18. I have taught in SEND schools for three years before joining Seadown. I enjoy playing Hockey on the weekend and have a passion for football and F1.
In my role as SENCo, I bring a strategic, pupil-centred approach to the staff governor role, ensuring that SEND considerations are embedded in all school decisions. I bring a strong track record of collaborative leadership with teaching teams, support staff, parents, and external agencies, which will help bridge gaps between policy and practice. My experience overseeing EHCPs, evaluating intervention effectiveness, and implementing targeted strategies means I can advocate effectively for resource allocation, staff training, and timely progress monitoring.
If you are interested in becoming a governor of Seadown School please contact the Clerk, Nikki Orchard at nikki.orchard@seadownschool.co.uk

Seadown School
Sports Leaders
Our Sports leaders are pupil volunteers who assist with the delivery of sport across the school. They support in the planning and delivery of Sports day, they take ideas from the pupils on how to improve and expand sport across Seadown. Sports leaders are challenged to take an active leadership role with sport at Seadown. They are great role models to other pupils across school.
Our sports leaders will complete training with Hugh MacGregor (SENCo) and can be spotted around school with their sports leader hoodies.

Seadown School
Local Offer & SEND Information
Seadown School is an independent SEN school for pupils aged 6 to 16. We are registered for 31 pupils.
All of the pupils in attendance have been referred to us via a local authority’s Dynamic Placement System. Children and young people who have previously been isolated at, or excluded from, school are supported to grow and develop socially, to gain some confidence and be encouraged to do their personal academic best.
The school can provide provision for a variety of additional Special Educational Needs and we offer a holistic and nurturing approach to education. All staff are experienced in working with young people with a variety of educational needs including ASC, ADHD, trauma and attachment, SEMH, moderate learning difficulties and dyslexia.

Seadown School
Careers Education & Guidance
The school arrange for an external careers coach to make an annual visit. During this visit there is a whole class presentation followed by an individual meeting for all the students in our two secondary school age classes.
After each visit the careers coach produces a career action plan for each student.
As a school, we support our year 11 pupils with identifying college courses and the transition to their chosen college.

Seadown School
Community Links
Seadown School is situated in an enviable location, close to the beach and town centre of Worthing, and within a stone’s throw of the South Downs, all of which provide a wealth of wonderful resources right on our doorstep! We continue to build fantastic links with a range of businesses and charities within our locality to support and enrich learning experiences and opportunities for our pupils. Some of our key partnerships include:
Splashpoint Leisure Centre
Worthing Leisure Centre
St George’s Church Hall
The Stables at Cissbury
Big Al’s Fitness/South Coast Gym
YourSpace – Play Therapy

Elite Tutors - Dyslexia tutor & GCSE Maths Tutor)
PAWS (People and Animal Wellbeing Services)

West Sussex County Council
Brighton & Hove County Council

If your organisation could support the life and learning our pupils, please do contact us office@seadownschool.co.uk

Seadown School
Physical activities:
Physical actives are a key part of school life here at Seadown, important for both physical and emotional health. We look to incorporate movement throughout our school day with pupils’ engagement in the Daily Mile, sensory activities, movement breaks and sensory circuits are also being available to pupils.
Each week pupils participate in a physical activity, whether that be swimming lessons, trampolining, or Forest Schools. In addition, there are further active opportunities for pupils to take part in, including personal training, boxing and horse riding. At the end of every term, classes enjoy an active day trip out that they themselves choose. Examples our pupils have enjoyed so far include, Fishers Farm Park, Out of Bounds, Laserquest, Jumpin Fun, Lodge Hill and Flip Out.
Our pupils enjoy joining other schools for active events such as football tournaments and MENCAP fun day. Our Sports Leaders help organise activities for our annual Sports day.
Onsite we have a fantastic trim trail and football area for our pupils and a great range of equipment for use at outside break and lunchtime. We are excited about the creation of our new hall as part of our building work, which will further extend our physical activities offer through options such as yoga and dance.

Seadown School
SMSC & British Values
At Seadown School we actively promote the fundamental British values (democracy, the rule of law, individual liberty, and mutual respect and tolerance for different faiths and beliefs) as part of their Spiritual, Moral, Social and Cultural (SMSC) development. These values sit alongside our school values (Respect, Cooperate, Curiosity, Resilience) and prepare pupils for life in modern Britain and is embedded through the curriculum, assemblies, and the school ethos.
How we promote British Values via SMSC:
Democracy: Implementing a school council, allowing pupils to voice opinions, and holding mock elections to teach about democratic processes.
· Rule of Law: Teaching pupils the importance of rules and laws, including the school behaviour policy, and understanding the consequences of breaking them.
· Individual Liberty: Promoting resilience, self-esteem, and self-confidence while encouraging pupils to take responsibility for their behaviour.
· Mutual Respect and Tolerance: Fostering an understanding of different cultures, religions, and beliefs to encourage respect.

Seadown School
Feel Good Friday Clubs
These take place every Friday afternoon where the pupils put their name down to take part in the club of their choice. These clubs are off curriculum and based on suggestions made by the pupils, through the school council, or by the school staff.

Seadown School
Our Curriculum
Seadown School believes that a flexible curriculum model best meets the changing needs of pupils. This ensures all pupils access learning appropriate for their age and stage of development. Learning is differentiated by cognitive level and need using a range of appropriate strategies and content which is designed to support teaching and learning for our cohorts.
Facilitating key learning and life skills enables pupils to transition successfully through the school and into adult life.
Seadown School believes that a flexible curriculum model best meets the changing needs of pupils. This ensures all pupils access learning appropriate for their age and stage of development.
The school as an expectation that the following subjects are taught across all classes weekly:
English (reading, writing, speaking & communication). Key support includes Read Write INC, VIPERS and Hamilton Brookes
Mathematics – White Rose forms the basis of our teaching and learning
PSHCE (Personal, Social, Health education) which includes Spiritual, Moral, Social, and Cultural Development & British Values.
The school provides a scheme of work for all these areas and the content is adapted in line with the needs of the pupils. Purple Mash and Hamilton Brookes support learning in Computing and Science.
Read, Write Inc is the scheme used to teach phonics at Seadown School. All teachers and support staff in our lower school classes have completed training. Using a phonics scheme aids consistency of teaching approach, which gives pupils the best chance of success when learning to read.
Phonics is taught on a daily basis in our lower primary class and pupils in our upper primary class are supported on a 1:1 basis with either our Academic Tutor or one of our trained TAs.
As pupils move through the school the focus is on engagement and enjoyment of reading and exploring books. The expectation is to read and understand more complex texts as pupils develop a more detailed knowledge of vocabulary and grammar.
If you would like to find out more about Read Write Inc please visit https://www.ruthmiskin.com/
The wider curriculum
The school offers a broad and balanced curriculum that over the year will give all students access to a wide range of curriculum subjects including:
A modern foreign language
The content is designed to inspire curiosity and is tailored to the interests of the cohort. These subjects are block taught across the year and are reviewed by the teacher with a progression map of curriculum skills. Purple Mash and Hamilton Brookes support our teaching in these areas.
Following consultation with our School Council, across an academic year, our pupils have access to the following physical activities:
Lower school: Swimming for 2 terms and Forest Schools for one term
Upper school: Swimming for 1 term, trampolining for 1 term and Forest Schools for 1 term
Each class also participates in the daily mile in our local community.
We assess pupils in a variety of different ways both formatively and summatively.
Phonics: pupils are assessed on a regular basis using our ReadWrite Inc assessment system
Maths: White Rose assessment activities are incorporated into learning
Other subjects: We have worked with teachers to devise our own assessment system based on a set of “I can” statements that have been created to assess progress in:
Cognitive and practical skills
Personal and social skills
Functional Skills exams
ASDAN short course portfolios
We track progress in core learning and the wider curriculum on a termly basis and this data, alongside pupil books and pupil voice is discussed at termly pupil progress meetings to inform next steps in learning and support/intervention.
Parents/carers are kept up to date with their child’s progress formally through parent/carer – teacher consultations in the autumn and spring. Parents/carers receive reports in the autumn and summer. Parents/carers also receive a weekly communication covering key highlights of the week.

Seadown School
School Closure Procedure
In the event of school closure, for example for emergencies linked to weather, heating or water issues etc, our decision will be communicated to you as promptly as possible and by 7:30am wherever possible. The decision to close temporarily will be made by the Headteacher in conjunction with the Senior Leadership and Directors following a risk assessment process, subject to a number of factors.
This decision will be communicated with you in the following ways:
By Arbor (email) alert
On our school website
In the event of a school closure we will contact local authority school Transport Teams. There are a number of communications we need to make to ensure all relevant stakeholders are informed of a school closure. For this reason we ask that you do not contact the school office or individual members of staff to ask if the school will be open or not as this will delay the communication process to relevant parties.
In the event of a closure, we will provide information as soon as possible regarding re-opening information. Wherever possible you will be provided with details of remote learning.

Seadown School
Pupil Premium
Pupil premium is an allocation of money given to schools to improve the educational outcomes for disadvantaged pupils. These include pupils who are looked after by the local authority, those who have been eligible for Free School Meals at any point in the last six years (also known as Ever 6 FSM) and for children whose parents are currently serving in the armed forces. Students who are cared for by the local authority also receive a monetary allocation called Pupil Premium Plus.
In order to ensure the effective use of our PPG (Pupil Premium Grant), we use a range of strategies linked to evidence such as those evaluated by the Education Endowment Foundation (EEF). Our use of the pupil premium grant is linked to evidence-informed activities in line with the ‘menu of approaches’ set by the Department for Education (DfE), a 3-tiered approach, in which our spending is allocated across the following areas:
developing high-quality teaching, e.g. through professional development and recruitment and retention
providing targeted academic support, such as one-to-one or small group tuition
tackling non-academic barriers to academic success, such as difficulties with attendance, behaviour and social and emotional wellbeing
To be eligible for pupil premium or recovery premium, pupils must be:
Currently eligible for free school meals (FSM) or have been eligible for FSM at any point in the last 6 years
Looked after by the local authority
Previously looked after by the local authority or other state care.
Eligibility for Free School Meals
Your child may be able to get free school meals if you get any of the following:
income-related Employment and Support Allowance
support under Part VI of the Immigration and Asylum Act 1999
the guaranteed element of Pension Credit
Child Tax Credit (provided you’re not also entitled to Working Tax Credit and have an annual gross income of no more than £16,190)
Working Tax Credit run-on - paid for 4 weeks after you stop qualifying for Working Tax Credit
Universal Credit - if you apply on or after 1 April 2018 your household income must be less than £7,400 a year (after tax and not including any benefits you get)
Children who get paid these benefits directly, instead of through a parent or guardian, can also get free school meals.
Your child may also get free school meals if you get any of these benefits and your child is both:
younger than the compulsory age for starting school
in full-time education
If you do not qualify for most benefits (also known as having ‘no recourse to public funds’), your child may still be eligible for free school meals.
Please contact our school secretary for further details and for support with checking your child’s eligibility.

Seadown School
Message from the Head
Welcome to Seadown School. It is a privilege to be Headteacher of our small, caring, independent special school for pupils aged 6 to 16, where we celebrate every pupil as an individual. Our pupils have a range of neurodiverse needs including ASC, ADHD, dyslexia and DCD. Our provision also supports pupils with SEMH needs (social, emotional and mental health).
We pride ourselves on forming positive, trusting and respectful relationships with pupils where everyone is valued. We work closely with families and see positive home-school relationships as an important part in ensuring each pupil thrives and reaches their full potential.
Seadown seeks to remove barriers to learning, providing a nurturing environment through a trauma-informed, attachment aware approach to support mental health and wellbeing. Our teaching and learning aims to engage and inspire, building on children’s interests, prior knowledge and skills. Alongside academic studies, our curriculum incorporates a structured life skills element. This approach is underpinned by our strong values work, helping prepare our pupils to become independent and responsible individuals, equipping them for their chosen pathway and to flourish in the wider community.
Our highly skilled and caring team provide a wide variety of support including tailored interventions to address gaps in learning, as well as pastoral interventions aimed at developing pupils’ social and emotional development. We also work with a wide variety of partners who lead interventions onsite linked directly to their EHCPs. A wide range of offsite activities and interventions enrich our provision supporting pupils’ holistic development.
I would be delighted to welcome you to Seadown and share with you what makes our popular and successful school, a special place to grow and learn.

pageCache.pageTitle: Our Vision, Mission and Values | Seadown School
pageCache.text:
Seadown School
Our Vision, Mission and Values
We know and value each of our pupils as individuals, Pupils’ learning journeys are designed to ensure progress with academic and life skills to support pupils to learn without limits, within a safe, welcoming and inclusive environment. Strong links with home and our wider community help foster pupils’ sense of belonging.
We strive to create an inclusive, nurturing environment that encourages and enhances each pupil’s uniqueness. We aim to engage hearts and minds through personalised teaching and learning that inspires, building the confidence to try new things and the resilience to face and overcome challenges. Positive relationships are central to our pupil’s success. We aim to support every pupil to achieve their full potential and equip them with the life skills they need to thrive as valued members of our community and wider society.
Our school values, agreed with all members of our school, underpin our school's ethos, guide our behaviour, and influence our teaching and learning. Our Seadown values help foster a positive community, promote character development and support a sense of belonging.
Pupils demonstrating our school values are recognised in our weekly Celebration assemblies and also through our Weekly Updates to parents/carers.

Seadown School
School Council at Seadown School
Milo (representing Puffer Fish Class)
What does a School Council do?
A school council is a formal group of pupils who act as representatives of their classmates in discussing school issues with the deputy headteacher and staff. It’s a brilliant way of representing and contributing to the Pupil Voice in our school.
Pupils are elected to represent the views of all pupils and also to improve their school. They help to make decisions about key aspects of the school and take on projects that support the children’s learning and development such as: making improvements to the school, organising charity events, representing the school at outside events or ensuring the school is environmentally friendly. School councils are elected annually by the other children.
Why do we have a School Council?
There are lots of reasons to have a school council. Article 12 of the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child (UNCRC) says that children and young people should have a say in decisions that affect their lives. A school council can provide a meaningful way in which pupils can voice their opinions and have their views taken into account in decisions that impact upon them. Evidence and experience from schools all over the country shows that a school council that is supported and nurtured helps to improve many aspects of school life. It is an important and useful way for schools to provide leadership and development opportunities for their pupils.
Student councils are a great way for pupils to take on leadership roles, promote the voice of the student body, problem solve and impact their community. The curriculum requires that young people are provided with opportunities to participate in school and society. School councils are an excellent way in which to increase participation, teaching young people about democracy, local and global citizenship and accountability.
Key roles of our School Council
School council members must be able to:
1. Represent their year group at school council meetings with commitment and full attendance.
2. Report back to their class following school council meetings.
3. Believe in the importance of representing their year group’s point of view (even if they do not agree with it themselves.)
4. Initiate discussion and debate with fellow student representatives and understand the importance of teamwork.
5. Understand that as a school council representative, they have the obligation to participate in making decisions about the school, along with staff and school governors.

Seadown School
Our Staff
Our staff team are highly experienced in the provision of education for pupils who are unable to work within a mainstream setting. They have a wealth of special education experience and support regulation through a trauma informed and attachment aware approach.
We place strong emphasis on supporting our staff through relevant continuing professional development to ensure our pupils thrive academically, socially and emotionally.
